To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SANC package is able to compute the one-loop electroweak radiative corrections to the decay rates of the Z(H,W) bosons into the fermions, and the corresponding differential distributions.

we have developed a computer system for automatic calculation of the pseudo- and real observables for a variety of processes of particle interaction in the one-loop and two-loop approximations, which is capable of calculating the decay rate of Z(H,W) bosons into fermions and the corresponding distributions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a system of computer programs, which will allow to calculate, in the one-loop precision, the decay rates and distributions for the decaying processes of the Z(H,W) bosons, the t t production and the decays of the Higgs bosons.

the development of the SANC computer system, which will automatically compute, at the one- and higher-loop precision levels, the pseudo- and observable quantities, for the processes of elementary particle interactions, using the principle and the methods of knowledge storing.
the development of the computer system SANC (former CalePHEP) which is aimed at the theoretical analysis and support of the experiments at modern and new colliders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SANC is a very promising project which is being developed and is already capable of producing very interesting results.

we have a working system for the calculation of the one-loop electroweak radiative corrections to the processes of the elementary particles interactions, which can be easily extended to other processes and other physics models.
the program is ready to compute one-loop corrections to any process with any number of external particles, and with any number of particles in the intermediate states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the system is ready to compute the decay rates and distributions for the decay of Z(H,W) to fermions, and the decay rates for the decay of the Higgs to the fermions and the bosons in one-loop approximation.
the system is ready to be applied to any processes of elementary particle interactions, and the only thing that is needed is a description of the corresponding processes in the language of SANC.
the system has been created, tested, and is now ready for the calculations of realistic observables at the one-loop level.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the results of the SANC calculation for the decay Z(H,W)→ f f are in agreement with the results of FeynArts, FormCalc, LoopTools and GRACE up to 11 significant digits, and the results obtained with SANC for the decay W → f f are in good agreement with the results obtained by other groups.

the SANC system can be used to compute one-loop amplitudes in the Standard Model and its extensions, as well as to calculate the decay rates and distributions for any process with arbitrary number of external lines.
the SANC package is a useful tool for the theoretical predictions of realistic observables at the one-loop level.
